app.page.aboutUs.header: Petropavl Express Logistics cooperates with a wide network of partners in the territories of the CIS countries, Latvia, Lithuania, Estonia, and Georgia.
app.page.aboutUs.paragraph1: The young and dynamically developing transport company “Petropavl Express Logistics” has been operating in the forwarding services market since 2010. In the competitive regional market, we managed to quickly capture a significant share and become one of the fastest-growing transport companies in Kazakhstan.
app.page.aboutUs.paragraph2: We are proud of the high performance indicators that have brought Petropavl Express Logistics to the forefront and look to the future with optimism.
app.page.aboutUs.paragraph3: The experience, knowledge, and reputation we have gained over the years allow us to set higher goals. We have achieved this through consistent improvement in transportation efficiency, continuous implementation and development of new technologies, and the quality of services that have increased our partners’ loyalty.
app.page.aboutUs.paragraph4: **The company’s main value** is our team. Each specialist is a professional in their field. These are the people who helped the company reach its current heights and continue to drive its growth and leadership.
app.page.aboutUs.paragraph5: The cohesive teamwork and effective management system allow us to seize opportunities for further development.

app.page.containers.paragraph1: Containers are mainly intended for the transportation of packaged and piece goods without additional packaging. The MPS fleet has a large number of universal containers with a gross weight of 1.25, 3, and 5 tons. Heavy-duty all-metal containers with a gross weight of 10, 20, and 30 tons are becoming widespread on railways. Containers with a gross weight of 1.25 tons are now made of metal with a welded body reinforced on a wheeled frame.
app.page.containers.paragraph2: The front wheels are mounted on a common axle and turn by means of a drawbar. To brake the container, the drawbar is set in a vertical position, in which the wheels are clamped by brake pads. On the wide side of the container, there is a double-leaf door with a lock. The container’s tare weight is 193 kg, and the body volume is 1.125 m³.
app.page.containers.paragraph3: Containers with a gross weight of 3 tons of all-metal construction have five closed trough-shaped frame ribs on the body, measuring 60x50x3 mm. The ribs are covered on the inside with a smooth metal sheet 1.5 mm thick.
app.page.containers.paragraph4: Lifting eyes for slinging are located in roof recesses. The front wall is made as a double-leaf door, with a lock mounted on the right leaf. To prevent moisture from entering the container, the door leaves are equipped with an additional gutter. Corner supports (legs) 100 mm high allow the use of a forklift truck. The container’s tare weight is 585 kg, and the body volume is 5.12 m³.
app.page.containers.paragraph5: Containers with a gross weight of 5 tons and a metal body are equipped with four closed load-bearing ribs.
app.page.containers.paragraph6: The door leaves — left and right — are mounted on hinges. The lock is located on the right door. The roof and outer sheathing are made of 1.5 mm thick steel sheet. Lifting eyes for hoisting the container are placed in recesses. The legs allow the container to be moved with a forklift. The container’s tare weight is 1100 kg, and the body volume is 10.2 m³.
app.page.containers.paragraph7: The inner walls of all containers are made smooth to prevent cargo damage.
app.page.containers.paragraph8: All-metal containers are strong enough to be transported in stacks. All new all-metal containers are equipped with lifting eyes (hooks) that allow for automatic slinging during loading and unloading by cranes.
app.page.containers.paragraph9: Since containers are transported by all types of transport, their overall dimensions, gross weight, and fastening devices must strictly comply with State Standards and international regulations.

app.page.dangerousGoods.header1: Classification and labeling under ADR are divided into the following classes:
app.page.dangerousGoods.paragraph1: Dangerous goods include any substances, materials, products, or waste from industrial or other activities that, due to their properties and characteristics, may pose a threat to human life and health, harm the environment, or damage or destroy material assets during transportation.
app.page.dangerousGoods.paragraph10: **CLASS 7** — radioactive substances with a specific activity greater than 70 kBq/kg (2 nCi/g).
app.page.dangerousGoods.paragraph11: **CLASS 8** — corrosive substances that cause skin damage, affect mucous membranes of the eyes and respiratory tract, corrode metals, damage transport vehicles, structures, or goods, and may ignite when in contact with organic materials or certain chemicals; **Subclass 8.1** — acids; **Subclass 8.2** — alkalis; **Subclass 8.3** — other corrosive substances.
app.page.dangerousGoods.paragraph12: **CLASS 9** — substances of relatively low transport hazard not included in previous classes but requiring specific transport and storage rules; **Subclass 9.1** — solid and liquid combustible substances and materials that do not belong to Classes 3 and 4 but may pose a fire hazard under certain conditions (combustible liquids with a flash point from +61°C to +100°C in a closed cup, fibers, and other similar materials); **Subclass 9.2** — substances that become corrosive under certain conditions.
app.page.dangerousGoods.paragraph2: According to GOST 19433-88, dangerous goods are classified as hazardous.
app.page.dangerousGoods.paragraph3: Dangerous goods of each class are divided into subclasses, categories, and groups according to their physical and chemical properties, types, and degrees of hazard during transportation, as defined by GOST 19433-88.
app.page.dangerousGoods.paragraph4: **CLASS 1** — explosive materials capable of detonating or causing fire with an explosive effect, as well as devices containing explosives or initiating means designed to produce pyrotechnic effects; **Subclass 1.1** — explosive and pyrotechnic materials and products with mass explosion hazard; **Subclass 1.2** — explosive and pyrotechnic materials and products without mass explosion hazard; **Subclass 1.3** — explosive and pyrotechnic materials and products with fire hazard and minor explosive effect or none; **Subclass 1.4** — explosive and pyrotechnic materials and products presenting minor explosion hazard only in case of ignition or initiation, not causing device or package destruction; **Subclass 1.5** — explosive substances with mass explosion hazard that are so insensitive that detonation during transport is unlikely; **Subclass 1.6** — articles containing extremely insensitive substances with no mass explosion hazard and a very low probability of accidental initiation.
app.page.dangerousGoods.paragraph5: **CLASS 2** — compressed, liquefied (by cooling), and dissolved gases under pressure that meet at least one of the following conditions:
app.page.dangerousGoods.paragraph6: **CLASS 3** — flammable liquids, mixtures of liquids, and liquids containing solids in solution or suspension that emit flammable vapors with a flash point of 61°C or below in a closed cup; **Subclass 3.1** — highly flammable liquids with a flash point below −18°C or with other hazardous properties; **Subclass 3.2** — moderately flammable liquids with a flash point from −18°C to +23°C; **Subclass 3.3** — flammable liquids with a flash point from +23°C to +61°C inclusive.
app.page.dangerousGoods.paragraph7: **CLASS 4** — flammable substances and materials (excluding those classified as explosives) capable of igniting easily during transport due to external ignition sources, friction, moisture absorption, spontaneous chemical reactions, or heating; **Subclass 4.1** — flammable solids that ignite easily and burn intensely; **Subclass 4.2** — self-igniting substances that may spontaneously heat up and ignite under normal transport conditions; **Subclass 4.3** — substances that emit flammable gases when in contact with water.
app.page.dangerousGoods.paragraph8: **CLASS 5** — oxidizing substances and organic peroxides capable of easily releasing oxygen, supporting combustion, or, under certain conditions or in mixtures, causing self-ignition and explosion; **Subclass 5.1** — oxidizing substances that are not flammable themselves but promote combustion and increase fire intensity; **Subclass 5.2** — organic peroxides, most of which are flammable, act as oxidizers, and can dangerously react with other substances. Many ignite easily and are sensitive to shock and friction.
app.page.dangerousGoods.paragraph9: **CLASS 6** — toxic and infectious substances capable of causing death, poisoning, or disease when ingested, inhaled, or in contact with skin or mucous membranes; **Subclass 6.1** — toxic substances that can cause poisoning by inhalation (vapors, dust), ingestion, or skin contact; **Subclass 6.2** — substances and materials containing pathogenic microorganisms hazardous to humans and animals.

app.page.paymentRailwayTariffs.paragraph: Direct agreements with JSC ‘Russian Railways’ and JSC ‘NC KTZ’ for tariff payments allow us to provide our clients with railway tariff payment services in Russia and Kazakhstan on favorable terms.

Our company has a direct agreement with Latvian Railways for tariff payment on cargo transportation through land border crossings and seaports of Latvia. This agreement allows us to offer our clients advantageous cooperation conditions.

Payment of railway tariffs is an essential part of cargo transportation by rail. When handling tariff payments, we also provide complimentary services: we inform clients about delivery times along selected routes, pay the tariff in case of cargo redirection, track shipments, and resolve other tariff-related matters.

app.page.schema.header: The loading scheme of wagons usually includes the following sections:
app.page.schema.paragraph1: Cargo with different characteristics and dimensions requires special handling techniques and technologies during loading operations. There are several regulatory documents that govern the loading process. They define the conditions for securing and placing various types of cargo on different types of rolling stock. For transportation across foreign territories, specific loading and placement regulations also apply.
app.page.schema.paragraph2: The scheme is a mandatory document ensuring the proper procedure for placing and securing cargo. Before the loading scheme is approved by Russian Railways, it must be approved by the shipper.
app.page.schema.paragraph3: Petropavl Express Logistics specialists prepare sketches and drawings of the loading scheme according to your cargo’s characteristics.
app.page.schema.paragraph4: After document preparation, the loading scheme is coordinated with representatives of Russian Railways and Kazakhstan Temir Zholy.
app.page.schema.paragraph5: The overall efficiency of the transportation process largely depends on how accurately the loading scheme is developed. Our clients — shippers — do not need to study this issue on their own; they can simply use our loading scheme coordination service.
app.page.schema.title: Development and Coordination of Loading Schemes

app.page.wagons.paragraph1: All wagons consist of the following main components: the body with frame, running gear, automatic couplers, and braking equipment. The body serves to accommodate passengers or cargo.
app.page.wagons.paragraph2: **The body design depends on the purpose of the wagon.** The frame of a freight covered wagon consists of metal posts, arches, and beams made of shaped steel profiles. The walls are sheathed with steel sheets. If wooden panels are used, the frame has additional metal braces. The roof arches and framing are covered with steel sheets welded together to form a solid metal roof. Previously, roofs were made of roofing steel without loading hatches and were less durable. The body has one or two sliding all-metal doors on each side and two hatches on each longitudinal wall.
app.page.wagons.paragraph3: The frame of an all-metal passenger wagon body is a single welded load-bearing metal structure consisting of transverse and longitudinal beams and posts, as well as roof arches. The outer cladding and roof are made of corrugated steel sheets welded to the frame. Such a body is stronger and lighter per passenger seat.
app.page.wagons.paragraph4: The interior partitions and wall linings are made of wood, fiberboard, and polymer materials. The base of the body — the frame — absorbs longitudinal impact and traction forces acting on the wagon and supports the cargo weight. The central beam of the frame in modern freight wagons consists of two heavy steel channels or I-beams spaced to accommodate the coupler assembly. Both beams are joined with steel plates, forming a single robust structure. The central beam is connected to end (buffer) beams, crossbeams, and pivot beams, which are joined by side beams. The design of the frame in open wagons or tank cars allows installation of discharge hatches or a tank.
app.page.wagons.paragraph5: The body rests on running gear that transfers the wagon and cargo weight to the rails. The running gear includes wheelsets, axle boxes with bearings, and the spring suspension. In four- and multi-axle wagons, these elements are combined into bogies, providing smoother travel and easier passage through curves.
app.page.wagons.paragraph6: The main type of freight wagon bogie is the two-axle TsNII-Kh3 bogie with single-stage spring suspension. It consists of two cast side frames with openings for spring assemblies. The axle box housings of the wheelsets are inserted into the side frame slots. The cast bolster is a box-section beam that carries the load from the wagon through the center plate connection. The beam ends rest on wedge dampers and spring sets.
app.page.wagons.paragraph7: The wedges are placed in special recesses and contact steel replaceable plates fixed on the side frames. Depending on the wagon’s load, each spring set consists of five to seven double-row springs. The wheelsets have a rolling circle diameter of 950 mm. Brake hangers with brake shoes are mounted on brackets of the side frames and connected to vertical levers and the brake rigging. For six-axle wagons, triple-axle bogies are used, and for eight-axle wagons, double two-axle articulated bogies of the TsNII-Kh3 type.
app.page.wagons.paragraph8: Some freight wagons still have two-axle bogies with axle boxes cast as one with the side frames, and belt-type bogies, which are gradually being replaced by TsNII-Kh3 type bogies. The two-axle KVZ-TsNII bogie is the most advanced type for passenger wagons. Its welded frame rests on cylindrical springs above the axle boxes, which in turn rest on roller bearing supports. The bogie features a central suspension system consisting of four triple-row springs, two cradle beams, four hangers, and side hydraulic dampers.
app.page.wagons.paragraph9: Bogie sets for wagons with a gross weight up to 70 tons have one hydraulic damper per side, while heavier wagons have two per side. Older all-metal passenger wagons used central cradle suspension with elliptical springs and no hydraulic dampers, allowing speeds up to 120 km/h.
app.page.wagons.title: General Information on Wagon Construction
app.page.wagonsTypes.header2: Isothermal wagons are used to transport perishable goods.
app.page.wagonsTypes.paragraph1: The wagon fleet consists of two main groups of wagons — passenger and freight.
app.page.wagonsTypes.paragraph10: For transporting bulk cargo, industrial enterprises use dump cars. These are equipped with pneumatic systems that tilt the body for unloading.
app.page.wagonsTypes.paragraph11: For this purpose, refrigerated wagons with mechanical cooling are used. These are combined into trains or sections of 23, 12, or 5 units. Some wagons house electric and refrigeration equipment. Autonomous refrigerated wagons with individual cooling and electric heating are becoming increasingly common. There are also ice-cooled isothermal wagons (ice wagons), as well as special wagons for transporting live fish, wine, and other products.
app.page.wagonsTypes.paragraph2: These wagons differ by the number of axles, load capacity, and suitability for certain types of cargo. On the railways of the former USSR, four-, six-, and eight-axle wagons, as well as multi-axle special wagons, are used. The main freight fleet consists of four-axle wagons. The construction of heavy eight-axle open wagons and tank cars is expanding. Depending on the cargo type, wagons are divided into covered, open, platform, tank, isothermal, and special-purpose types.
app.page.wagonsTypes.paragraph3: **Covered wagons** are designed for transporting valuable and weather-sensitive goods such as grain, packaged goods, and others. The metal walls have side hatches, and the steel roof has four loading hatches with automatic locks.
app.page.wagonsTypes.paragraph4: The all-metal self-sealing body doors have unloading hatches at the bottom for partially unloading grain to relieve door pressure before opening. Door sealing is achieved using rubber gaskets of special profiles and grooves at the thresholds. Self-sealing door wagons can carry grain without using grain shields. Older four-axle covered wagons use wooden shields in doorways when carrying grain.
app.page.wagonsTypes.paragraph5: **Open wagons** make up a significant portion of the freight wagon fleet and are used most intensively. They have no roof, and the floor has discharge hatches with locking mechanisms. Open wagons are designed for bulk cargo such as ore, coal, metal, machinery, etc., not requiring weather protection. This type allows for mechanized loading and unloading, including wagon tippers. For heavy cargo on busy routes, heavy-duty eight-axle open wagons are used.
app.page.wagonsTypes.paragraph6: **Flatcars** are used for transporting long cargo (rails, lumber), containers, vehicles, and various machines. The four-axle all-metal flatcar is the standard type.
app.page.wagonsTypes.paragraph7: Tank cars transport liquid bulk cargo, primarily petroleum products. Depending on the product, tanks are equipped with top or bottom discharge systems. The tank body is cylindrical with a dome on top and safety valves for gasoline transport. Tank cars with a 62-ton capacity and universal discharge devices are used for gasoline and light oil products.
app.page.wagonsTypes.paragraph8: **Grain wagons** are four-axle all-metal covered wagons with sloped walls forming hoppers that serve as grain containers and facilitate unloading. The roof has hermetically sealed loading hatches.
app.page.wagonsTypes.paragraph9: Similar specialized wagons exist for transporting cement and pellets. The four-axle hopper-doser is used for crushed stone transport and is equipped with a dosing mechanism, convenient for track works.
app.page.wagonsTypes.title: Main Types of Wagons
